original_paragraph.Experimental Section - Protein Preparati: The extracellular domain of human toll-like receptor 8 (hTLR8, residues 27–827) was prepared as described previously.4 ITC experiments were performed in a buffer composed of 25 mM MES pH 5.5, 0.20 M NaCl, and 5% DMSO at 298 K using a MicroCal iTC200 (GE Healthcare). The titration sequence included a single 0.4 μL injection followed by 18 injections, 2 μL each, with a spacing of 120 s between the injections. The titration conditions were as follows: 100 μM R848 into 10 μM hTLR8 and 50 μM CU-68; 100 μM R848 into 10 μM hTLR8 and 50 μM CU-72; 100 μM R848 into 10 μM hTLR8 and 50 μM CU-115.
original_paragraph.Figure 8 caption: Figure 8. Therapeutic potential of CU-115, CU-72, and CU-68 on NF-κB inhibition mediated by ssRNA-stimulated HEK 293-TLR8 cells. HEK 293 cells, hTLR8 cells, and an inducible SEAP reporter gene were incubated with sample compounds for 16 h. The data were normalized as [(raw data – untreated cells)/(ligand + solvent control – untreated cells)]. Ligand + solvent is 100% activation, and untreated cells are 0% activation. At 5 μM, CU-68 suppresses the NF-κB inhibition induced by ssRNA-Lyo-40 in HEK 293 TLR8 cells, while CU-115 and CU-72 displayed weaker activity (data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 independent experiments). (b) CU-68 dose-response-dependent NF-κB inhibition mediated by ssRNA-stimulated HEK 293-TLR8 cells (data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 independent experiments). (c) ITC thermogram of CU-68 titrated into hTLR8 to determine binding affinity. The titration of R848 into hTLR8 premixed with CU-68 (left), and the titration of R848 into hTLR8 alone (right), suggesting that CU-68 prevents R848 from binding to TLR8 (representative of one independent experiment). The raw data are presented on the top, and the integrated peak areas are shown and fitted below.
